docs.title: OpenMembraneBuilder
docs.text:
Build Martini coarse-grained membranes and membrane–protein systems – in the browser or from the command line – ready to simulate with GROMACS. Choose the lipids of every leaflet, prepare and place your proteins, and get structure, topology, force field, simulation settings and a run script for every system.

Get started Your first system config.json reference

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
• Membranes – any mixture of the lipids shipped with Martini 3 or Martini 2.2, different in the two leaflets, given as fractions or as exact numbers of lipids, typed in or loaded from a template.
  • Proteins – upload coarse-grained files, or start from an atomistic structure (your own file or a PDB code) that is cleaned, cut to the chains and residues you want, optionally mutated, and converted with martinize2. Each protein gets a name of your choice.
  • Placement – put every protein where you want it: position, height (absolute, or a gap above the membrane), rotation, random placements, several copies moving together or each on its own – and see the result in a schematic system view before building.
  • Replicas – build up to 99 independent systems at once, with the same or with different random protein placements.
  • Ready for GROMACS – each build contains the force field, the topology with clean includes, the minimisation/equilibration/production settings and a run.sh that runs them for every system.
  • Reproducible – every build writes a config.json; omb cli config.json builds the same systems again, on your laptop or on a cluster.

docs.title: Citing
docs.text: If OpenMembraneBuilder helps your research, please cite it together with COBY and martinize2.

docs.title: Installation and commands
docs.text:
• Installable with pip – from the repository (pip install .) or from a single file (openmembranebuilder-2.0.0.tar.gz / .whl); all dependencies, including martinize2 (vermouth), are installed with it.
  • One command for everything: omb gui, omb cli config.json, omb --version (also python -m openmembranebuilder …).
  • Builds are written to the folder omb is started from, or to $OMB_WORKDIR.
  • The code lives in the openmembranebuilder package (formerly src/); force fields, mdp files, scripts and templates are installed with it. streamlit run app.py and python app.py --no-gui config.json still work.

docs.title: Run the simulations from the app
docs.text:
• ▶ Run simulations on the results page starts systems/run.sh in the background after a build, with its log, a refresh and a stop button.
  • omb gui --no-run (or OMB_NO_RUN=1) hides it, for apps offered on web servers.

docs.title: Protein insertion
docs.text:
• System view: box, membrane and proteins in x–z, y–z and x–y, drawn from the real protein beads and rotated exactly as COBY places them; warnings when a protein sticks out of the box or proteins overlap.
  • The box can be changed on the protein insertion page.
  • Copies of a protein can move together (grid) or independently, each with its own position and rotation.

docs.title: Proteins and topology
docs.text:
• Every protein gets a name (e.g. 1UBQ): its files are <name>.pdb / <name>.itp, and the topology lists it as <name> ([ moleculetype ] and [ molecules ]).
  • Copies of one protein are included once and counted in one line of [ molecules ].

docs.title: Fixes
docs.text:
• config.json is included in the download zip; omb cli also writes it to the output.
  • index.sh reads the current config.json format, so run.sh creates the index groups.
  • Protein rotations follow COBY's convention (x, then y, then z about the turned axes).

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text: • Every module, class and function explained in plain language; this documentation site with user guide, references and code reference.

• Command-line builds from a saved config.json.
  • config.json written with every build and included in the zip archive.
  • Temporary upload folders removed after each build.
  • Cardiolipin lipids (TMCL, TOCL).
  • Self-contained output folders with copies of the input files (user_inputs/).

docs.title: Contributing to OpenMembraneBuilder
docs.text:
OpenMembraneBuilder is an open-source community-driven platform focused on reproducible, extensible, and collaborative scientific workflows and infrastructure.

We welcome contributions from developers, researchers, testers, and designers.

docs.title: Ways to Contribute
docs.text: Contributions can broadly be divided into two categories:

docs.title: 1. Testing and Validation
docs.text:
Testing is a critical part of the project and includes:

  • bug reporting
  • workflow validation
  • benchmarking
  • documentation improvements
  • reproducibility checks
  • platform compatibility testing
  • usability feedback

Scientific software quality strongly depends on rigorous testing and validation from the community.

docs.title: 2. Module and Feature Development
docs.text:
We also welcome technical contributions such as:

  • new modules
  • workflow integrations
  • UI/UX improvements
  • API integrations
  • visualization components
  • documentation systems
  • deployment tooling

The project is designed to evolve modularly, and community-developed components are highly encouraged.

docs.title: Academic Contribution and Authorship
docs.text:
OpenMembraneBuilder is developed with an open-science philosophy.

Major contributors to the project may be recognized through authorship in associated academic manuscripts and preprints, depending on the scope and significance of their contributions.

docs.title: Living Preprint Model
docs.text:
The project aims to maintain a continuously updated preprint accompanying major releases of the platform.

For each major release:

  • contributors may be acknowledged or included as co-authors
  • release-specific contributions may be documented
  • major technical and scientific advancements may be summarized

This creates a transparent and evolving record of community contributions.

docs.title: Future Journal Submission
docs.text:
As the platform matures and stabilizes, we plan to submit an associated manuscript to a peer-reviewed scientific journal (e.g. methods- or infrastructure-oriented journals).

The goal is to establish OpenMembraneBuilder as:

  • a robust scientific platform
  • a reproducible open framework
  • a sustainable community-driven infrastructure

docs.title: How a click becomes a build
docs.text:
Streamlit redraws the whole page after every click. The pages therefore follow one pattern:

  1. gui.py draws the widgets. A button only leaves a short note in the session memory (for example _membrane_action = "next") and asks for a redraw.
  2. page.py reads the note on the redraw, copies the widget values into the builder's config.py object, checks them and moves to the next page.
  3. runner.py does the actual work from the config object alone – which is why omb cli can run the same code from a config.json without any page.
sequenceDiagram
    participant U as You
    participant G as gui.py
    participant P as page.py
    participant C as Config
    participant R as runner.py
    U->>G: press "Next →"
    G->>G: note "next", redraw
    P->>C: copy widget values
    P->>P: check, go to next page
    U->>G: press "🔨 Build"
    P->>R: run(config)
    R-->>P: systems + zip

docs.title: cli
docs.text:
The omb command, the single entry point of OpenMembraneBuilder.

omb gui [--port 8501] [streamlit options]   start the graphical interface in the browser
omb gui --no-run                            the same, without the "Run simulations" button
omb cli config.json                         rebuild the systems of a saved config.json (no GUI)
omb --version                               print the installed version

omb gui starts Streamlit with the wizard page; any option that omb itself does not know (for example --server.headless true) is passed on to Streamlit unchanged.

omb gui --no-run hides the button that starts the simulations after a build – use it when the app is offered to others, e.g. on a web server, so that nobody can run programs on it.

omb cli reads a config.json written by an earlier build and builds the same systems again, without opening a browser – handy for scripts, clusters and batch work.

Everything the program writes (the output/ and downloads/ folders) goes to the folder the command is started from, or to the folder named by the OMB_WORKDIR environment variable.

def _version() -> str:
    """The installed version of OpenMembraneBuilder, as recorded by pip.

    Returns:
        The version text, e.g. `"2.0.0"`, or a short note when the package is used
        without being installed (for example straight from a source folder).
    """
    try:
        return version("OpenMembraneBuilder")
    except PackageNotFoundError:
        return "unknown (not installed)"

def main(argv=None) -> int:
    """Run the `omb` command.

    Reads the command line, then either starts the graphical interface (`gui`) or rebuilds
    the systems of a configuration file (`cli`).

    Args:
        argv: The command-line words after `omb`. Leave empty to use the real command line;
            tests pass a list such as `["cli", "config.json"]`.

    Returns:
        The exit code: `0` when everything went well, `3` when the configuration file does
        not exist, otherwise the exit code of Streamlit.
    """
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="omb", description="OpenMembraneBuilder: Martini membrane and membrane–protein systems with COBY")
    parser.add_argument("--version", action="version", version=f"OpenMembraneBuilder {_version()}")
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)
    g = sub.add_parser("gui", help="start the graphical interface (Streamlit) in the browser")
    g.add_argument("--port", type=int, default=None, help="port of the web server (default 8501)")
    g.add_argument("--no-run", action="store_true",
                   help="hide the 'Run simulations' button (e.g. when the app is offered on a web server)")
    c = sub.add_parser("cli", help="build the systems of a config.json without the GUI")
    c.add_argument("config", help="config.json written by an earlier build")
    args, extra = parser.parse_known_args(argv)

    if args.cmd == "gui":
        app = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "app.py")
        cmd = [sys.executable, "-m", "streamlit", "run", app]
        if args.port:
            cmd += ["--server.port", str(args.port)]
        env = dict(os.environ)
        if args.no_run:  # read by the results page (wizard/run_simulations.py)
            env["OMB_NO_RUN"] = "1"
        return subprocess.call(cmd + extra, env=env)  # extra: any other `streamlit run` option

    if extra:
        parser.error(f"unrecognized arguments: {' '.join(extra)}")
    if not os.path.exists(args.config):
        print(f"Error: {args.config} not found", file=sys.stderr)
        return 3
    from openmembranebuilder.wizard.runner import run_from_config
    run_from_config(args.config)
    return 0

docs.title: core
docs.text:
Shared helpers used by all parts of the program.

  • global_info – where shipped data is found and where results are written.
  • filemanager – copying files into an output and creating the zip archive.
  • gui – the common page layout.

docs.title: global_info
docs.text:
Where OpenMembraneBuilder finds its own files and where it writes yours.

Two kinds of locations are used:

  • Shipped data – force fields (toppar), simulation settings (mdp), run scripts, membrane templates and example files. They live inside the installed package (openmembranebuilder/resources/), so they are found wherever the package is installed.
  • Your results – the output/ folder with the built systems, the downloads/ folder with the zip archives, and a temporary folder for uploaded files. They are created in the working folder: the folder where omb gui / omb cli was started, or the folder named by the environment variable OMB_WORKDIR.

docs.title: filemanager
docs.text:
Copying files into a build's output folder and packing the result into a zip archive.

Every build gets the same set of supporting files next to the systems: the force field, the simulation settings, the run scripts and copies of the files you uploaded. The FileManager puts them in place and, at the end, packs the whole folder into downloads/<folder>.zip.

copy_ff_folder(ff_name: str, destination: str)

Copy one force field (its folder of .itp files) into the output.

An older copy in the destination is removed first, so the output always holds exactly the shipped version.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default ff_name str

The output's toppar folder.

required Source code in openmembranebuilder/core/filemanager.py 
def copy_ff_folder(self, ff_name: str, destination: str):
    """Copy one force field (its folder of `.itp` files) into the output.

    An older copy in the destination is removed first, so the output always holds exactly
    the shipped version.

    Args:
        ff_name: Name of the force field, e.g. `"martini_v3"`.
        destination: The output's `toppar` folder.
    """
    src_folder = os.path.join(self.global_info.toppar_folder_path, ff_name)
    dst_folder = os.path.join(destination, ff_name)

    src_itp = os.path.join(self.global_info.toppar_folder_path, f"{ff_name}.itp")
    dst_itp = os.path.join(destination, f"{ff_name}.itp")

    if os.path.exists(dst_folder):
        shutil.rmtree(dst_folder)
    if os.path.exists(dst_itp):
        os.remove(dst_itp)

    if os.path.exists(src_folder):
        shutil.copytree(src_folder, dst_folder, dirs_exist_ok=True)
    if os.path.exists(src_itp):
        shutil.copy(src_itp, dst_itp)

def copy_mdp_files(self, ff_name: str, destination: str, system_type: str):
    """Copy the simulation settings (`em.mdp`, `eq1.mdp`, … `md.mdp`) into `<output>/mdp`.

    Args:
        ff_name: Name of the force field, e.g. `"martini_v3"`.
        destination: The output folder.
        system_type: `"membrane"` for membrane-only systems, `"protein"` when the system
            contains proteins (these settings couple protein and membrane together).
    """
    src_mdp = os.path.join(self.global_info.mdp_folder_path, ff_name, system_type)
    dst_mdp = os.path.join(destination, "mdp")
    if os.path.exists(src_mdp):
        os.makedirs(dst_mdp, exist_ok=True)
        for file in os.listdir(src_mdp):
            shutil.copy(os.path.join(src_mdp, file), os.path.join(dst_mdp, file))

Copy the run scripts into the output.

run.sh goes into <output>/systems (it runs every replica found there) and the helper index.sh, which creates the index groups, goes into <output>/scripts.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default destination str

The output folder.

required Source code in openmembranebuilder/core/filemanager.py 
def copy_scripts(self, destination: str):
    """Copy the run scripts into the output.

    `run.sh` goes into `<output>/systems` (it runs every replica found there) and the
    helper `index.sh`, which creates the index groups, goes into `<output>/scripts`.

    Args:
        destination: The output folder.
    """
    src_scripts = self.global_info.scripts_folder_path
    dst_scripts = os.path.join(destination, "systems")

    if os.path.exists(src_scripts):
        shutil.copytree(src_scripts, dst_scripts, dirs_exist_ok=True)

    # Move helper scripts to output/scripts
    src_index = os.path.join(dst_scripts, "index.sh")
    dst_index_dir = os.path.join(destination, "scripts")

    if os.path.exists(src_index):
        os.makedirs(dst_index_dir, exist_ok=True)
        shutil.move(src_index, os.path.join(dst_index_dir, "index.sh"))

def create_zip_folder(self, folder_path: str) -> str:
    """Pack a whole output folder into a zip archive in the downloads folder.

    Args:
        folder_path: The output folder of the build.

    Returns:
        The full path of the zip file, e.g. `downloads/OpenMembraneBuilder-<time>.zip`.
    """
    folder_path = Path(folder_path)

@staticmethod
def add_to_zip(zip_path: str, file_path: str, arcname: str | None = None) -> None:
    """Add one file to an existing zip archive, replacing an older copy of it.

    Used for `config.json`, which is written after the zip has been created.
    Nothing happens when the zip or the file does not exist.

    Args:
        zip_path: The zip archive to update.
        file_path: The file to add.
        arcname: Name of the file inside the zip; by default its own file name.
    """
    import zipfile
    if not (zip_path and os.path.exists(zip_path) and os.path.exists(file_path)):
        return
    arcname = arcname or os.path.basename(file_path)
    with zipfile.ZipFile(zip_path) as zf:
        present = arcname in zf.namelist()
    if present:  # rewrite the zip without the old copy
        tmp = zip_path + ".tmp"
        with zipfile.ZipFile(zip_path) as src, zipfile.ZipFile(tmp, "w", zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as dst:
            for item in src.infolist():
                if item.filename != arcname:
                    dst.writestr(item, src.read(item.filename))
        os.replace(tmp, zip_path)
    with zipfile.ZipFile(zip_path, "a", zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as zf:
        zf.write(file_path, arcname)

def copy_userinput(self, file_path, user_inputs_dir):
    """Keep a copy of a file you provided in the output's `user_inputs` folder.

    Args:
        file_path: The uploaded or prepared file.
        user_inputs_dir: The output's `user_inputs` folder (created when missing).

    Returns:
        The path of the copy.
    """
    os.makedirs(user_inputs_dir, exist_ok=True)
    new_file_path = os.path.join(user_inputs_dir, os.path.basename(file_path))
    if os.path.abspath(file_path) != os.path.abspath(new_file_path):
        shutil.copy2(file_path, new_file_path)
    return new_file_path

def render_page(title: str, content_fn, sidebar_fn=None,
                layout: str = "centered", sidebar_only: bool = False):
    """Draw one complete page: title, sidebar and content.

    After the page is drawn, Streamlit is told to stop, so nothing below this call is
    shown on the same page.

    Args:
        title: Page title, shown at the top and in the browser tab.
        content_fn: Function that draws the main area of the page.
        sidebar_fn: Function that draws the sidebar, or `None` for a page without one.
        layout: `"centered"` for a narrow page, `"wide"` to use the full browser width.
        sidebar_only: Draw only the title and the sidebar, without the main area.
    """
    st.markdown(
        """<style>
        div[data-testid="stBottom"] {
            position: fixed; bottom: 0; left: 0; right: 0;
            background: white; padding: 1rem 2rem;
            border-top: 1px solid #e0e0e0; z-index: 999;
        }
        </style>""",
        unsafe_allow_html=True,
    )
    st.set_page_config(page_title=title, layout=layout)
    if sidebar_fn is not None:
        with st.sidebar:
            sidebar_fn()
    st.title(title)
    if content_fn and not sidebar_only:
        st.divider()
        content_fn()
    st.stop()

def __post_init__(self):
    """Turn proteins read from a JSON file into `ProteinConfig` objects.

    Settings that older versions of the program stored but no longer use are ignored.

    Raises:
        TypeError: A protein entry is neither a dictionary nor a `ProteinConfig`.
    """
    converted_proteins: List[ProteinConfig] = []

    for item in self.proteins:
        if isinstance(item, dict):
            # ignore keys of older config versions (e.g. the removed copy_number)
            converted_proteins.append(ProteinConfig(**{k: v for k, v in item.items() if k in _PROTEIN_FIELDS}))
        elif isinstance(item, ProteinConfig):
            converted_proteins.append(item)
        else:
            raise TypeError(f"Unexpected type for protein entry: {type(item)}")

    self.proteins = converted_proteins
    self.n_proteins = len(self.proteins)

def protein_file_names(self) -> List[Optional[str]]:
    """The file name each finished protein gets in the membrane builder.

    Returns:
        One name per protein (e.g. `"1UBQ.pdb"`), in the order of `proteins`; `None` for
        proteins that are not finished. Should two files have the same name, the second is
        renamed so both are kept.
    """
    import os
    names: List[Optional[str]] = []
    used = set()
    for i, pc in enumerate(self.proteins):
        if not pc.output_cg_pdb_path or not pc.output_itp_path:
            names.append(None)
            continue
        name = os.path.basename(pc.output_cg_pdb_path)
        if name in used:  # same file name twice -> keep both, unique names
            name = f"p{i}_{name}"
        used.add(name)
        names.append(name)
    return names

def protein_files(self) -> Dict[str, Dict[str, str]]:
    """The finished proteins, as the membrane builder expects them.

    Only the current proteins are listed, so a deleted or re-run protein never leaves an
    old entry behind.

    Returns:
        `{"1UBQ.pdb": {"pdb_path", "itp_path", "force_field"}}`; `force_field` is
        `"martini_v3"`, `"martini_v2.2"` or empty when unknown.
    """
    files: Dict[str, Dict[str, str]] = {}
    for name, pc in zip(self.protein_file_names(), self.proteins):
        if name:
            files[name] = {
                "pdb_path": pc.output_cg_pdb_path,
                "itp_path": pc.output_itp_path,
                "force_field": martini_ff_of(pc) or "",
            }
    return files

def martini_ff_of(pc: "ProteinConfig") -> Optional[str]:
    """The membrane force field a protein belongs to.

    Args:
        pc: The protein's settings.

    Returns:
        `"martini_v3"`, `"martini_v2.2"`, or `None` when unknown (uploaded files without a
        stated generation).
    """
    if pc.protein_input_mode == "martinize":
        ff = (pc.forcefield or "").lower()
        if ff.startswith("martini3"):
            return "martini_v3"
        if ff.startswith("martini2"):      # martini22, martini22p
            return "martini_v2.2"
        return None
    v = (pc.cg_martini_version or "").strip()
    if v.endswith("3"):
        return "martini_v3"
    if v.endswith("2"):
        return "martini_v2.2"
    return None

def main(temp_folder: str) -> tuple[str | None, Config | None]:
    """Show the protein preparation; called by the wizard on every redraw.

    Args:
        temp_folder: The session folder for uploads and work files.

    Returns:
        `("done", config)` when all proteins are ready, `("back", None)` when the user
        leaves backwards, otherwise `(None, None)`.
    """
    runner = MartinizeRunner()

    # Initialise top-level config once. build_mode is always "protein_membrane"
    # here — the wizard already decided a protein is needed before routing here.
    if "martinize_config" not in st.session_state:
        st.session_state.martinize_config = Config(build_mode="protein_membrane")
    config: Config = st.session_state.martinize_config
    config.build_mode = "protein_membrane"

    temp_dir = Path(temp_folder) / "protein_input"
    temp_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    step        = _get_step()
    protein_idx = _get_protein_idx()

    if step == MartinizeStep.INPUT:
        return _render_input_step(config, runner, temp_folder)

    elif step == MartinizeStep.CONFIGURE:
        return _render_configure_step(config, runner, protein_idx, temp_folder)

    elif step == MartinizeStep.RESULTS:
        return _render_results_step(config, runner, protein_idx, temp_folder)

    return None, None

def _render_input_step(
    config: Config,
    runner: MartinizeRunner,
    temp_folder: str,
) -> tuple[str | None, Config | None]:

    # ── Handle add / delete / fetch signals (set by gui.py before st.rerun) ──
    """The input page: add, delete and download proteins, then check and continue.

    On "Next" every protein must have a valid, unique name and its files. Proteins from
    an atomistic structure continue to the configure page; coarse-grained uploads go
    straight to the results page.

    Args:
        config: The settings of all proteins.
        runner: The worker that downloads, cleans and converts structures.
        temp_folder: The session folder.

    Returns:
        `("back", None)` when leaving backwards, otherwise `(None, None)`.
    """
    if st.session_state.pop("_martinize_add_protein", False):
        config.proteins.append(ProteinConfig())
        config.n_proteins = len(config.proteins)
        st.session_state.martinize_config = config
        st.rerun()

    delete_idx = st.session_state.pop("_martinize_delete_protein", None)
    if delete_idx is not None and 0 <= delete_idx < len(config.proteins):
        names = [st.session_state.get(f"protein_name_p{k}", pc.name) for k, pc in enumerate(config.proteins)]
        names.pop(delete_idx)
        for k in range(len(config.proteins)):
            st.session_state.pop(f"protein_name_p{k}", None)
        for k, nm in enumerate(names):
            st.session_state[f"protein_name_p{k}"] = nm
        config.proteins.pop(delete_idx)
        config.n_proteins = len(config.proteins)
        st.session_state.martinize_config = config
        st.rerun()

    fetch_idx = st.session_state.pop("_martinize_fetch_requested", None)
    if fetch_idx is not None and 0 <= fetch_idx < len(config.proteins):
        pdb_id = st.session_state.get(f"fetch_pdb_id_p{fetch_idx}", "").strip()
        temp_dir = Path(temp_folder) / "protein_input"
        temp_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        try:
            with st.spinner(f"Downloading {pdb_id} from RCSB..."):
                path = runner.fetch_pdb(pdb_id, str(temp_dir))
            prev = st.session_state.get(f"atomistic_path_p{fetch_idx}", "")
            if prev != path:
                _reset_downstream_state(fetch_idx)
            st.session_state[f"atomistic_path_p{fetch_idx}"] = path
            st.session_state[f"fetched_pdb_success_p{fetch_idx}"] = f"Successfully fetched PDB: {pdb_id}"
        except Exception as e:
            st.error(f"Error fetching PDB: {e}")

    # ── Handle navigation action ──────────────────────────────────────────────
    action = st.session_state.pop("_martinize_input_action", None)

    if action == "back":
        return "back", None

    if action == "next":
        # Ensure at least one protein is defined
        if not config.proteins:
            st.error("Please add at least one protein before proceeding.")
        else:
            # Harvest all proteins from session_state into config
            for i, pconfig in enumerate(config.proteins):
                _harvest_input_to_pconfig(pconfig, i, runner, temp_folder)

            # Validate all proteins
            all_errors = []
            for i, pconfig in enumerate(config.proteins):
                for err in _validate_input(pconfig, i):
                    all_errors.append(f"Protein {i+1}: {err}")
            names = [pc.name.lower() for pc in config.proteins if pc.name]
            dup = sorted({n for n in names if names.count(n) > 1})
            if dup:
                all_errors.append(f"Each protein needs its own name ({', '.join(dup)} is used more than once).")
            if all_errors:
                for err in all_errors:
                    st.error(err)
            else:
                _invalidate_outputs()   # inputs may have changed -> results must be recomputed
                # Go to the configure step if input mode is martinize, else go to the result step
                first_input_mode = config.proteins[0].protein_input_mode
                if first_input_mode == "martinize":
                    _load_chain_data(config.proteins[0], 0, runner)
                    _set_protein_idx(0)
                    _set_step(MartinizeStep.CONFIGURE)
                else:
                    # All proteins are pre-built CG — go straight to results for protein 0
                    _set_protein_idx(0)
                    _set_step(MartinizeStep.RESULTS)
                st.rerun()

    render_input(config, temp_folder)
    return None, None

def _render_configure_step(
    config: Config,
    runner: MartinizeRunner,
    protein_idx: int,
    temp_folder: str,
) -> tuple[str | None, Config | None]:
    """The configure page of one protein: DSSP preview, Back, or check and run.

    Args:
        config: The settings of all proteins.
        runner: The worker.
        protein_idx: Position of the protein.
        temp_folder: The session folder.

    Returns:
        Always `(None, None)`; the page changes by itself.
    """
    pconfig = config.proteins[protein_idx]
    p = protein_idx
    action = st.session_state.pop("_martinize_configure_action", None)

    if action == "dssp_preview":
        active = st.session_state.get(f"active_struct_p{p}", "")
        if active:
            try:
                with st.spinner("Calculating DSSP secondary structure..."):
                    result = runner.get_secondary_structure_mdtraj(active)
                st.session_state[f"dssp_preview_result_p{p}"] = result
            except Exception as e:
                st.session_state[f"dssp_preview_error_p{p}"] = str(e)

    elif action == "back":
        # Go back: if this is the first martinize protein, back to INPUT
        _set_step(MartinizeStep.INPUT)
        st.rerun()

    elif action == "run":
        _harvest_configure_to_pconfig(pconfig, p)
        errors = _validate_configure(pconfig)
        if errors:
            for err in errors:
                st.error(f"Protein {p+1}: {err}")
        else:
            config.proteins[p] = pconfig
            st.session_state.martinize_config = config
            # Move to RESULTS for this protein (settings changed -> recompute)
            _invalidate_outputs([p])
            _set_protein_idx(p)
            _set_step(MartinizeStep.RESULTS)
            st.rerun()

    chains    = st.session_state.get(f"chains_p{p}", [])
    summaries = st.session_state.get(f"chain_summaries_p{p}", {})
    render_configure(pconfig, protein_idx, chains, summaries)
    return None, None

def _render_results_step(
    config: Config,
    runner: MartinizeRunner,
    protein_idx: int,
    temp_folder: str,
) -> tuple[str | None, Config | None]:
    """Run one protein and show the outcome.

    The work runs once per visit; coming back to the page shows the stored result. On
    success you continue to the next protein or, after the last one, to the membrane
    builder. On failure you can go back and fix the settings, or drop the protein.

    Args:
        config: The settings of all proteins.
        runner: The worker.
        protein_idx: Position of the protein.
        temp_folder: The session folder.

    Returns:
        `("done", config)` after the last protein, otherwise `(None, None)`.
    """
    p = protein_idx
    pconfig = config.proteins[p]
    is_last = (p == len(config.proteins) - 1)

    # ── Run the preprocessor once per protein visit ────────────────────────
    building_key = f"_martinize_building_p{p}"
    output_key   = f"martinize_output_p{p}"

    # run only if there is no stored result (coming back here must not silently re-run)
    if st.session_state.get(building_key, output_key not in st.session_state):
        # work inside the session temp folder: no intermediate output folders
        pconfig.base_folder = os.path.join(temp_folder, "martinize", f"p{p}")
        shutil.rmtree(pconfig.base_folder, ignore_errors=True)
        with st.spinner(f"Executing martinize2 workflow for protein {p+1}..."):
            output = runner.run(config, protein_index=p)

        if output.get("success"):
            outputs = output.get("outputs", {})

            pconfig.output_cg_pdb_path = outputs.get("cg_pdb_path", "")
            pconfig.output_itp_path = outputs.get("itp_path", "")

            # Make sure the updated ProteinConfig is stored in the top-level config
            config.proteins[p] = pconfig
            st.session_state.martinize_config = config

        st.session_state[output_key] = output
        st.session_state[building_key] = False


    output = st.session_state.get(output_key, {})

    st.title(f"🧬 Martinize Results — Protein {p + 1}")

    if output.get("success"):
        outputs = output["outputs"]
        st.success(f"✅ Martinize preprocessor executed successfully for protein {p+1}!")
        st.write(f"- **Coarse-grained PDB:** `{outputs.get('cg_pdb_path')}`")
        st.write(f"- **Topology ITP/TOP:** `{outputs.get('itp_path')}`")

        if "command" in outputs:
            with st.expander("Martinize2 Command Executed"):
                st.code(outputs["command"], language="bash")
        if "log" in outputs:
            with st.expander("Martinize2 Log Output"):
                st.code(outputs["log"])

        st.divider()
        if is_last:
            if st.button("Next: Membrane Builder ➡️", type="primary"):
                st.session_state.pop(building_key, None)
                return _finish(config)
        else:
            if st.button(f"Next protein ({p + 2} of {len(config.proteins)}) ➡️", type="primary"):
                st.session_state.pop(building_key, None)
                next_p = p + 1
                next_pconfig = config.proteins[next_p]
                if next_pconfig.protein_input_mode == "martinize":
                    _load_chain_data(next_pconfig, next_p, runner)
                    _set_protein_idx(next_p)
                    _set_step(MartinizeStep.CONFIGURE)
                else:
                    # upload_cg — skip configure, go straight to results
                    _set_protein_idx(next_p)
                    _set_step(MartinizeStep.RESULTS)
                st.rerun()

    else:
        st.error(f"❌ Martinize failed for protein {p+1}: {output.get('message')}")

        col_back, col_delete = st.columns(2)

        if col_back.button("← Go back and fix", use_container_width=True):
            st.session_state.pop(building_key, None)
            st.session_state.pop(output_key, None)
            _set_step(MartinizeStep.CONFIGURE)
            st.rerun()

        delete_label = (
            "🗑 Delete this protein & go to Membrane Builder"
            if is_last else
            f"🗑 Delete this protein & continue to protein {p + 2}"
        )
        if col_delete.button(delete_label, use_container_width=True):
            st.session_state.pop(building_key, None)
            _invalidate_outputs(range(p, len(config.proteins)))   # indices shift after the delete
            config.proteins.pop(p)
            config.n_proteins = len(config.proteins)
            st.session_state.martinize_config = config

            if not config.proteins:
                # No proteins left — send user back to input
                _set_protein_idx(0)
                _set_step(MartinizeStep.INPUT)
                st.rerun()
            elif p >= len(config.proteins):
                # Deleted the last protein; the new last one is done already
                if is_last:
                    # was the last → now go to membrane builder
                    return _finish(config)
                else:
                    _set_protein_idx(len(config.proteins) - 1)
                    _set_step(MartinizeStep.RESULTS)
                    st.rerun()
            else:
                # More proteins remain at index p
                next_pconfig = config.proteins[p]
                if next_pconfig.protein_input_mode == "martinize":
                    _load_chain_data(next_pconfig, p, runner)
                    _set_protein_idx(p)
                    _set_step(MartinizeStep.CONFIGURE)
                else:
                    _set_protein_idx(p)
                    _set_step(MartinizeStep.RESULTS)
                st.rerun()

    return None, None

def _invalidate_outputs(indices=None) -> None:
    """Forget stored results, so the proteins are run again when visited.

    Args:
        indices: Positions of the proteins to forget; all proteins when empty.
    """
    if indices is None:
        keys = [k for k in st.session_state.keys() if k.startswith("martinize_output_p")]
    else:
        keys = [f"martinize_output_p{i}" for i in indices]
    for k in keys:
        st.session_state.pop(k, None)

def reset_outputs(temp_folder: str) -> None:
    """Remove everything the protein preparation produced, keeping inputs and settings.

    Used when the user goes back into the protein preparation from a later step: work
    folders and results are deleted and the input page is shown again. The proteins are
    prepared again on the way forward.

    Args:
        temp_folder: The session folder.
    """
    shutil.rmtree(os.path.join(temp_folder, "martinize"), ignore_errors=True)

    config = st.session_state.get("martinize_config")
    if config is not None:
        for pc in config.proteins:
            pc.output_cg_pdb_path = ""
            pc.output_itp_path = ""
            pc.base_folder = ""

    for k in list(st.session_state.keys()):
        if k.startswith("martinize_output_p") or k.startswith("_martinize_building_p"):
            del st.session_state[k]
    st.session_state.pop("protein_files", None)

    _set_protein_idx(0)
    _set_step(MartinizeStep.INPUT)

def _harvest_input_to_pconfig(
    pconfig: ProteinConfig,
    i: int,
    runner: MartinizeRunner,
    temp_folder: str,
) -> None:
    """Copy the values of one protein's input panel into its settings.

    For atomistic structures with clean-up switched on, the cleaned structure is made
    here, so the configure page can show its chains.

    Args:
        pconfig: The protein's settings, changed in place.
        i: Position of the protein.
        runner: The worker (for the clean-up).
        temp_folder: The session folder.
    """
    pconfig.name               = str(st.session_state.get(f"protein_name_p{i}", pconfig.name)).strip()
    pconfig.protein_input_mode = st.session_state.get(f"protein_input_mode_p{i}", pconfig.protein_input_mode)
    pconfig.cg_martini_version = st.session_state.get(f"cg_version_p{i}",         pconfig.cg_martini_version)
    pconfig.atomistic_source   = st.session_state.get(f"atomistic_source_p{i}",   pconfig.atomistic_source)
    pconfig.fetch_pdb_id       = st.session_state.get(f"fetch_pdb_id_p{i}",       pconfig.fetch_pdb_id)
    pconfig.clean_structure    = st.session_state.get(f"clean_structure_p{i}",    pconfig.clean_structure)
    pconfig.cg_pdb_path        = st.session_state.get(f"cg_pdb_path_p{i}",        pconfig.cg_pdb_path)
    pconfig.cg_itp_path        = st.session_state.get(f"cg_itp_path_p{i}",        pconfig.cg_itp_path)

    if pconfig.protein_input_mode == "martinize":
        raw_path = st.session_state.get(f"atomistic_path_p{i}", "")
        pconfig.atomistic_pdb_path = raw_path

        if raw_path and pconfig.clean_structure:
            temp_dir = Path(temp_folder) / "protein_input"
            temp_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            if not st.session_state.get(f"cleaned_path_p{i}"):
                try:
                    cleaned = runner.clean_protein(raw_path, str(temp_dir), i)
                    st.session_state[f"cleaned_path_p{i}"] = cleaned
                except Exception as e:
                    st.error(f"Protein {i+1} cleaning failed: {e}")
            active = st.session_state.get(f"cleaned_path_p{i}") or raw_path
        else:
            active = raw_path

        st.session_state[f"active_struct_p{i}"] = active

def _validate_input(pconfig: ProteinConfig, i: int) -> list[str]:
    """Check one protein's input before continuing.

    Args:
        pconfig: The protein's settings.
        i: Position of the protein.

    Returns:
        The problems found (empty when all is well).
    """
    errors: list[str] = []
    if not pconfig.name:
        errors.append("Please give the protein a name (its files become <name>.pdb and <name>.itp).")
    elif not re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]*", pconfig.name):
        errors.append(f"Name '{pconfig.name}': use only letters, digits, _ and - (no spaces or dots).")
    if pconfig.protein_input_mode == "upload_cg":
        if not pconfig.cg_pdb_path or not os.path.exists(pconfig.cg_pdb_path):
            errors.append("Please upload a coarse-grained structure file (.pdb or .gro).")
        if not pconfig.cg_itp_path or not os.path.exists(pconfig.cg_itp_path):
            errors.append("Please upload a coarse-grained topology file (.itp).")
    elif pconfig.protein_input_mode == "martinize":
        if not st.session_state.get(f"atomistic_path_p{i}"):
            errors.append("Please upload or fetch an atomistic PDB structure.")
    return errors

def _validate_configure(pconfig: ProteinConfig) -> list[str]:
    """Check one protein's configuration before running martinize2.

    At least one chain is needed; a mutation needs chain, residue and new amino acid.

    Args:
        pconfig: The protein's settings.

    Returns:
        The problems found (empty when all is well).
    """
    errors: list[str] = []
    if pconfig.protein_input_mode == "martinize":
        if not pconfig.selected_chains:
            errors.append("Please select at least one chain.")
        if pconfig.do_mutation:
            if not pconfig.mutation_chain:
                errors.append("Mutation chain must be specified.")
            if pconfig.mutation_residue_idx is None:
                errors.append("Mutation residue must be specified.")
            if not pconfig.mutation_target:
                errors.append("Mutation target amino acid must be specified.")
    return errors

def _load_chain_data(pconfig: ProteinConfig, protein_idx: int, runner: MartinizeRunner) -> None:
    """Read the chains, their residue ranges and residue lists of one protein's structure.

    Args:
        pconfig: The protein's settings.
        protein_idx: Position of the protein.
        runner: The worker that reads the structure.
    """
    p = protein_idx
    active = st.session_state.get(f"active_struct_p{p}", "")
    if not active or not os.path.exists(active):
        st.session_state[f"chains_p{p}"]         = []
        st.session_state[f"chain_summaries_p{p}"] = {}
        return
    try:
        chains    = runner.get_chains(active)
        summaries = runner.get_chain_summary(active)
        st.session_state[f"chains_p{p}"]         = chains
        st.session_state[f"chain_summaries_p{p}"] = summaries
        for c in chains:
            key = f"residues_{c}_p{p}"
            if key not in st.session_state:
                st.session_state[key] = runner.get_residues_for_chain(active, c)
    except Exception as e:
        st.error(f"Could not load chains for protein {p+1}: {e}")
        st.session_state[f"chains_p{p}"]         = []
        st.session_state[f"chain_summaries_p{p}"] = {}

def render_input(config: Config, temp_folder: str) -> None:
    """Draw the protein input page.

    Shows one panel per protein (name, delete button, source, upload or download, clean-up),
    an "Add a protein" button and Back / Next.

    Args:
        config: The settings of all proteins.
        temp_folder: Folder where uploads are stored.
    """
    st.title("🧬 Protein Structure Input")
    st.caption("Provide the protein structures to be coarse-grained with martinize2.")

    temp_dir = Path(temp_folder) / "protein_input"
    temp_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    # ── One panel per protein ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
    for i, pconfig in enumerate(config.proteins):
        _render_protein_panel(i, pconfig, config.n_proteins, temp_dir)

    # ── Add a protein ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    st.divider()
    if st.button("➕ Add a protein", use_container_width=False):
        st.session_state["_martinize_add_protein"] = True
        st.rerun()

    # ── Navigation ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    with st.container(key="nav_martinize_input"):
        st.divider()
        left, _, right = st.columns([1, 6, 1])
        if left.button("← Back", use_container_width=True):
            st.session_state["_martinize_input_action"] = "back"
            st.rerun()
        if right.button("Next →", use_container_width=True, type="primary"):
            st.session_state["_martinize_input_action"] = "next"
            st.rerun()

        hdr_left.subheader(f"Protein {i + 1}")
        if hdr_right.button(
            "🗑 Delete", key=f"del_protein_{i}",
            use_container_width=True,
            help="Remove this protein from the workflow",
        ):
            st.session_state["_martinize_delete_protein"] = i
            st.rerun()

        # ── Name: the files become <name>.pdb and <name>.itp ──────────────────
        name_key = f"protein_name_p{i}"
        st.session_state.setdefault(name_key, pconfig.name)
        st.text_input(
            "Protein name",
            key=name_key,
            placeholder="e.g. 1UBQ",
            help="Required. The structure and topology files are named <name>.pdb and <name>.itp "
                 "(letters, digits, _ and -; each protein needs its own name).",
        )

        # ── Mode radio ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
        mode_key = f"protein_input_mode_p{i}"
        protein_input_mode = st.radio(
            "How do you want to provide the protein structure?",
            ["upload_cg", "martinize"],
            format_func=lambda x: {
                "upload_cg": "Upload already coarse-grained PDB/GRO + topology ITP",
                "martinize": "Start from atomistic PDB (Download from RCSB or Upload)",
            }[x],
            index=["upload_cg", "martinize"].index(
                st.session_state.get(mode_key, pconfig.protein_input_mode)
            ),
            key=mode_key,
        )

        st.divider()

        if protein_input_mode == "upload_cg":
            _render_upload_cg_panel(i, pconfig, temp_dir)
        else:
            _render_atomistic_panel(i, pconfig, temp_dir)

def _render_upload_cg_panel(i: int, pconfig: ProteinConfig, temp_dir: Path) -> None:
    """Upload fields for an already coarse-grained protein (structure + `.itp`).

    You also say which Martini generation the files are made for, so a mismatch with the
    membrane can be reported.

    Args:
        i: Position of the protein.
        pconfig: The protein's settings.
        temp_dir: Folder where uploads are stored.
    """
    st.subheader("Upload Coarse-Grained Protein Files")
    col1, col2 = st.columns(2)

    with col1:
        uploaded_cg_pdb = st.file_uploader(
            "Upload CG Structure (.pdb, .gro)", type=["pdb", "gro"],
            key=f"cg_pdb_uploader_p{i}",
        )
        if uploaded_cg_pdb:
            dest = str(temp_dir / f"p{i}_{uploaded_cg_pdb.name}")
            with open(dest, "wb") as f:
                f.write(uploaded_cg_pdb.getvalue())
            st.session_state[f"cg_pdb_path_p{i}"] = dest
            st.success(f"Uploaded: {uploaded_cg_pdb.name}")
        elif f"cg_pdb_path_p{i}" not in st.session_state:
            st.session_state[f"cg_pdb_path_p{i}"] = pconfig.cg_pdb_path

    with col2:
        uploaded_cg_itp = st.file_uploader(
            "Upload Protein Topology (.itp)", type=["itp"],
            key=f"cg_itp_uploader_p{i}",
        )
        if uploaded_cg_itp:
            dest = str(temp_dir / f"p{i}_{uploaded_cg_itp.name}")
            with open(dest, "wb") as f:
                f.write(uploaded_cg_itp.getvalue())
            st.session_state[f"cg_itp_path_p{i}"] = dest
            st.success(f"Uploaded: {uploaded_cg_itp.name}")
        elif f"cg_itp_path_p{i}" not in st.session_state:
            st.session_state[f"cg_itp_path_p{i}"] = pconfig.cg_itp_path

    version_options = ["unknown", "Martini 2", "Martini 3"]
    version_key = f"cg_version_p{i}"
    st.session_state.setdefault(version_key, pconfig.cg_martini_version if pconfig.cg_martini_version in version_options else "unknown")
    st.selectbox(
        "Martini version of these files",
        version_options,
        key=version_key,
        help="Used to warn you if the protein does not match the force field of the membrane. "
             "Martini 2 and Martini 3 models must not be mixed.",
    )

def _render_atomistic_panel(i: int, pconfig: ProteinConfig, temp_dir: Path) -> None:
    """Source of an atomistic structure: upload a PDB file or download one from RCSB.

    Loading a different structure resets the chain and mutation choices of this protein.
    The clean-up option keeps only the protein.

    Args:
        i: Position of the protein.
        pconfig: The protein's settings.
        temp_dir: Folder where uploads are stored.
    """
    st.subheader("Atomistic Structure Input")

    source_key = f"atomistic_source_p{i}"
    atomistic_source = st.radio(
        "Select atomistic structure source:",
        ["Upload PDB", "Fetch from PDB database"],
        index=["Upload PDB", "Fetch from PDB database"].index(
            st.session_state.get(source_key, pconfig.atomistic_source)
        ),
        key=source_key,
    )

    if atomistic_source == "Upload PDB":
        uploaded_at = st.file_uploader(
            "Upload Atomistic PDB File", type=["pdb"],
            key=f"atomistic_pdb_uploader_p{i}",
        )
        if uploaded_at:
            dest = str(temp_dir / f"p{i}_{uploaded_at.name}")
            with open(dest, "wb") as f:
                f.write(uploaded_at.getvalue())
            prev = st.session_state.get(f"atomistic_path_p{i}", "")
            if prev != dest:
                _reset_downstream_state(i)
            st.session_state[f"atomistic_path_p{i}"] = dest
            st.success(f"Uploaded: {uploaded_at.name}")
    else:
        col1, col2 = st.columns([3, 1])
        with col1:
            st.text_input(
                "Enter 4-letter RCSB PDB ID:",
                value=st.session_state.get(f"fetch_pdb_id_p{i}", pconfig.fetch_pdb_id),
                placeholder="e.g. 1UBQ",
                key=f"fetch_pdb_id_p{i}",
            )
        with col2:
            st.write(" ")
            st.write(" ")
            if st.button("Fetch Structure", type="primary", key=f"fetch_btn_p{i}"):
                pdb_id = st.session_state.get(f"fetch_pdb_id_p{i}", "").strip()
                if len(pdb_id) == 4:
                    st.session_state["_martinize_fetch_requested"] = i
                    st.rerun()
                else:
                    st.error("PDB ID must be exactly 4 characters.")

        if st.session_state.get(f"fetched_pdb_success_p{i}"):
            st.success(st.session_state[f"fetched_pdb_success_p{i}"])

    if st.session_state.get(f"atomistic_path_p{i}"):
        st.write(f"**Loaded structure:** `{st.session_state[f'atomistic_path_p{i}']}`")

    # Clean-up checkbox
    st.divider()
    st.subheader("Structure Clean-up")
    st.checkbox(
        "Clean structure with MDAnalysis (removes water, ligands, ions – keeps protein only)",
        value=st.session_state.get(f"clean_structure_p{i}", pconfig.clean_structure),
        key=f"clean_structure_p{i}",
    )

def render_configure(
    pconfig: ProteinConfig,
    protein_idx: int,
    chains: List[str],
    summaries: Dict[str, Any],
) -> None:
    """Draw the configure page of one protein.

    - **Chains**: tick the chains to keep and, per chain, the residue range.
    - **Mutation**: chain, residue (filterable by amino acid) and the new amino acid.
    - **martinize2 options**: force field, secondary structure (with a DSSP preview),
      elastic network, position restraints, disulfide bridges, extra options.

    Args:
        pconfig: The protein's settings.
        protein_idx: Position of the protein.
        chains: The chains found in the structure.
        summaries: Per chain: first and last residue and number of residues.
    """
    p = protein_idx  # shorthand for key namespacing

    st.title("⚙️ Configure & Martinize")
    st.caption(f"Protein {protein_idx + 1} — Select chains, configure mutations, and set martinize2 parameters.")

    # ── Chain selection ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    st.subheader("Chain Selection")

    new_selected: List[str] = []
    new_ranges: Dict[str, List[int]] = {}

    if chains:
        prev_selected: List[str] = st.session_state.get(
            f"selected_chains_p{p}", pconfig.selected_chains or chains
        )
        prev_selected = [c for c in prev_selected if c in chains]
        chain_ranges: Dict[str, List[int]] = st.session_state.get(
            f"chain_ranges_p{p}", dict(pconfig.chain_ranges)
        )

        hdr = st.columns([0.5, 1, 1.5, 1.5, 1.5, 1.5])
        hdr[0].markdown("**Select**")
        hdr[1].markdown("**Chain ID**")
        hdr[2].markdown("**# Residues**")
        hdr[3].markdown("**First ResID**")
        hdr[4].markdown("**Last ResID**")
        hdr[5].markdown("**Residue Range**")

        for c in chains:
            s = summaries.get(c, {})
            row = st.columns([0.5, 1, 1.5, 1.5, 1.5, 1.5])
            is_selected = row[0].checkbox(
                "sel", value=(c in prev_selected),
                key=f"chain_sel_{c}_p{p}", label_visibility="collapsed",
            )
            row[1].write(c)
            if s:
                row[2].write(str(s.get("n_residues", "—")))
                row[3].write(str(s.get("first_resid", "—")))
                row[4].write(str(s.get("last_resid", "—")))
            else:
                for col in row[2:5]:
                    col.write("—")

            if is_selected:
                new_selected.append(c)
                if s:
                    first_resid = s.get("first_resid", 1)
                    last_resid  = s.get("last_resid", 9999)
                    prev_range  = chain_ranges.get(c, [first_resid, last_resid])
                    prev_start  = prev_range[0] if prev_range and len(prev_range) == 2 else first_resid
                    prev_end    = prev_range[1] if prev_range and len(prev_range) == 2 else last_resid
                    rc = row[5].columns(2)
                    range_start = rc[0].number_input(
                        "From", min_value=first_resid, max_value=last_resid,
                        value=max(first_resid, min(last_resid, prev_start)),
                        key=f"chain_range_start_{c}_p{p}", label_visibility="collapsed",
                    )
                    range_end = rc[1].number_input(
                        "To", min_value=first_resid, max_value=last_resid,
                        value=max(first_resid, min(last_resid, prev_end)),
                        key=f"chain_range_end_{c}_p{p}", label_visibility="collapsed",
                    )
                    new_ranges[c] = [int(range_start), int(range_end)]
                else:
                    new_ranges[c] = []

        if not new_selected:
            st.warning("⚠️ Please select at least one chain.")

        st.session_state[f"selected_chains_p{p}"] = new_selected
        st.session_state[f"chain_ranges_p{p}"]    = new_ranges

    else:
        st.warning("No protein chains could be identified in the structure.")

    # ── Mutation ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    st.divider()
    st.subheader("Mutation")
    do_mutation = st.checkbox(
        "Introduce residue mutation",
        value=st.session_state.get(f"do_mutation_p{p}", pconfig.do_mutation),
        key=f"do_mutation_p{p}",
    )

    if do_mutation and new_selected:
        mutation_chain       = st.session_state.get(f"mutation_chain_p{p}",       pconfig.mutation_chain)
        mutation_residue_idx = st.session_state.get(f"mutation_residue_idx_p{p}", pconfig.mutation_residue_idx)
        mutation_target      = st.session_state.get(f"mutation_target_p{p}",      pconfig.mutation_target)

        if mutation_chain not in new_selected:
            mutation_chain = new_selected[0]

        hdr = st.columns([1.2, 1.2, 1.2, 1.2])
        hdr[0].markdown("**Chain ID**")
        hdr[1].markdown("**Amino acid**")
        hdr[2].markdown("**ResID**")
        hdr[3].markdown("**Mutant**")

        sel = st.columns([1.2, 1.2, 1.2, 1.2])

        mutation_chain = sel[0].selectbox(
            "Chain", options=new_selected,
            index=new_selected.index(mutation_chain),
            key=f"mut_chain_sel_p{p}", label_visibility="collapsed",
        )

        all_residues = st.session_state.get(f"residues_{mutation_chain}_p{p}", [])
        chosen_range = new_ranges.get(mutation_chain, [])
        if chosen_range and len(chosen_range) == 2:
            range_start_val, range_end_val = chosen_range
            range_residues = [r for r in all_residues if range_start_val <= r["resid"] <= range_end_val]
        else:
            range_residues = all_residues

        if range_residues:
            unique_names = sorted({r["resname"] for r in range_residues})
            aa_filter_opts = ["All"] + unique_names
            prev_aa_filter = st.session_state.get(f"mut_aa_filter_p{p}", "All")
            if prev_aa_filter not in aa_filter_opts:
                prev_aa_filter = "All"
            aa_filter = sel[1].selectbox(
                "AA filter", options=aa_filter_opts,
                index=aa_filter_opts.index(prev_aa_filter),
                key=f"mut_aa_filter_p{p}", label_visibility="collapsed",
            )

            visible_residues = range_residues if aa_filter == "All" else [
                r for r in range_residues if r["resname"] == aa_filter
            ]
            resid_list = [r["resid"] for r in visible_residues]

            if resid_list:
                if mutation_residue_idx not in resid_list:
                    mutation_residue_idx = resid_list[0]
                sel[2].selectbox(
                    "RESID", options=resid_list,
                    index=resid_list.index(mutation_residue_idx),
                    key=f"mut_resid_sel_p{p}", label_visibility="collapsed",
                )
                standard_aas = [
                    "ALA", "ARG", "ASN", "ASP", "CYS", "GLN", "GLU",
                    "GLY", "HIS", "ILE", "LEU", "LYS", "MET", "PHE",
                    "PRO", "SER", "THR", "TRP", "TYR", "VAL",
                ]
                sel[3].selectbox(
                    "Mutant", options=standard_aas,
                    index=standard_aas.index(mutation_target) if mutation_target in standard_aas else 0,
                    key=f"mut_target_sel_p{p}", label_visibility="collapsed",
                )
            else:
                st.warning(f"No residues of type **{aa_filter}** found in the selected range.")
        else:
            st.warning("No residues found in the selected range for this chain.")
    elif do_mutation and not new_selected:
        st.warning("⚠️ Select at least one chain above before configuring a mutation.")

    # ── Martinize2 Options ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    st.divider()
    st.subheader("Martinize Coarse-Graining Options")

    forcefield_opts = ["martini22", "martini3001", "martini3001-idp"]
    st.selectbox(
        "Force field (-ff):",
        forcefield_opts,
        index=forcefield_opts.index(st.session_state.get(f"forcefield_p{p}", pconfig.forcefield)),
        key=f"forcefield_p{p}",
    )

    ss_opts = ["MDTraj DSSP", "All coil", "None", "Custom/Precalculated"]
    st.selectbox(
        "Secondary structure mode:",
        ss_opts,
        index=ss_opts.index(st.session_state.get(f"secondary_structure_mode_p{p}", pconfig.secondary_structure_mode)),
        key=f"secondary_structure_mode_p{p}",
    )

    if st.session_state.get(f"secondary_structure_mode_p{p}") == "Custom/Precalculated":
        st.text_input(
            "Precalculated secondary structure string (-ss):",
            value=st.session_state.get(f"custom_ss_string_p{p}", pconfig.custom_ss_string),
            placeholder="e.g. HHHHCCCCCCEEEEEE",
            key=f"custom_ss_string_p{p}",
        )

    if st.session_state.get(f"secondary_structure_mode_p{p}") == "MDTraj DSSP":
        if st.button("Preview calculated DSSP sequence", key=f"dssp_btn_p{p}"):
            st.session_state["_martinize_configure_action"] = "dssp_preview"
            st.rerun()
        if f"dssp_preview_result_p{p}" in st.session_state:
            st.text_area(
                "DSSP String Preview:", value=st.session_state[f"dssp_preview_result_p{p}"],
                height=100, disabled=True, key=f"dssp_area_p{p}",
            )
            if f"dssp_preview_error_p{p}" in st.session_state:
                st.error(st.session_state.pop(f"dssp_preview_error_p{p}"))

    st.checkbox(
        "Enable elastic network (-elastic)",
        value=st.session_state.get(f"use_elastic_network_p{p}", pconfig.use_elastic_network),
        key=f"use_elastic_network_p{p}",
    )
    if st.session_state.get(f"use_elastic_network_p{p}", pconfig.use_elastic_network):
        c1, c2, c3 = st.columns(3)
        c1.number_input(
            "Lower cutoff (-el nm)", min_value=0.0, max_value=5.0, step=0.1,
            value=st.session_state.get(f"elastic_lower_p{p}", pconfig.elastic_lower),
            key=f"elastic_lower_p{p}",
        )
        c2.number_input(
            "Upper cutoff (-eu nm)", min_value=0.0, max_value=5.0, step=0.1,
            value=st.session_state.get(f"elastic_upper_p{p}", pconfig.elastic_upper),
            key=f"elastic_upper_p{p}",
        )
        c3.number_input(
            "Force constant (-ef)", min_value=0.0, max_value=10000.0, step=100.0,
            value=st.session_state.get(f"elastic_force_p{p}", pconfig.elastic_force),
            key=f"elastic_force_p{p}",
        )

    restraints_opts = ["none", "backbone", "all"]
    st.selectbox(
        "Position restraints (-p):",
        restraints_opts,
        index=restraints_opts.index(st.session_state.get(f"position_restraints_p{p}", pconfig.position_restraints)),
        key=f"position_restraints_p{p}",
    )

    cys_opts = ["auto", "detect", "none"]
    st.selectbox(
        "Cysteine bridges (-cys):",
        cys_opts,
        index=cys_opts.index(st.session_state.get(f"cysteine_bridges_p{p}", pconfig.cysteine_bridges)),
        key=f"cysteine_bridges_p{p}",
    )

    st.text_input(
        "Extra martinize2 options (space-separated):",
        value=st.session_state.get(f"extra_flags_p{p}", pconfig.extra_flags),
        placeholder="e.g. -maxwarn 5 -nt",
        key=f"extra_flags_p{p}",
    )

    # ── Navigation ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    with st.container(key="nav_martinize_configure"):
        st.divider()
        left, mid, right = st.columns([1, 3, 1])
        if left.button("← Back", use_container_width=True):
            st.session_state["_martinize_configure_action"] = "back"
            st.rerun()
        if mid.button("🧬 Run Martinize Preprocessor", use_container_width=True, type="primary"):
            st.session_state["_martinize_configure_action"] = "run"
            st.rerun()

def _reset_downstream_state(protein_idx: int) -> None:
    """Forget everything that depends on the loaded structure of one protein.

    Called when a new structure is uploaded or downloaded: chain choices, ranges,
    mutation, DSSP preview and residue lists no longer apply.

    Args:
        protein_idx: Position of the protein.
    """
    p = protein_idx
    for key in [
        f"cleaned_path_p{p}", f"fetched_pdb_success_p{p}",
        f"selected_chains_p{p}", f"chain_ranges_p{p}",
        f"do_mutation_p{p}", f"mutation_chain_p{p}",
        f"mutation_residue_idx_p{p}", f"mutation_residue_name_p{p}",
        f"mutation_target_p{p}", f"dssp_preview_result_p{p}",
        f"active_struct_p{p}", f"chains_p{p}", f"chain_summaries_p{p}",
    ]:
        st.session_state.pop(key, None)
    for key in list(st.session_state.keys()):
        if key.startswith(f"residues_") and key.endswith(f"_p{p}"):
            del st.session_state[key]

docs.title: runner
docs.text:
The protein preparation's work: download, clean, select, mutate, coarse-grain, name.

For an atomistic structure, MartinizeRunner.run_one_protein does, in this order:

  1. download it from RCSB (or take the uploaded file),
  2. keep only the protein (clean-up, optional),
  3. keep the chosen chains and residue ranges,
  4. mutate one residue with PyMOL (optional),
  5. run martinize2 (with the secondary structure from DSSP, an elastic network, … as chosen),
  6. copy the results to cg/<name>.pdb and cg/<name>.itp.

For already coarse-grained files only the last step is done, after a basic check of the files. A log, the settings and a zip of each protein's work folder are written as well.

def fetch_pdb(self, pdb_id: str, output_dir: str) -> str:
    """Download a structure from the RCSB PDB.

    Args:
        pdb_id: Four-character PDB code, e.g. `1UBQ`.
        output_dir: Where to save `<PDBID>.pdb`.

    Returns:
        The downloaded file.

    Raises:
        ValueError: The code could not be downloaded.
    """
    pdb_id = pdb_id.upper().strip()
    url = f"https://files.rcsb.org/download/{pdb_id}.pdb"
    response = requests.get(url)
    if response.status_code != 200:
        raise ValueError(f"Could not fetch PDB ID from RCSB: {pdb_id}")
    output_path = os.path.join(output_dir, f"{pdb_id}.pdb")
    with open(output_path, "w") as f:
        f.write(response.text)
    return output_path

def get_chains(self, input_path: str) -> List[str]:
    """The chain names of a structure (or segment names when chains are missing).

    Args:
        input_path: The structure.

    Returns:
        Chain names, sorted.

def get_chain_summary(self, input_path: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """First residue, last residue and number of residues of every chain.

    Args:
        input_path: The structure.

    Returns:
        `{chain: {first_resname, first_resid, last_resname, last_resid, n_residues}}`.
    """
    u = mda.Universe(input_path)
    summaries = {}
    for chain in self.get_chains(input_path):
        atoms = u.select_atoms(f"protein and chainID {chain}")
        if len(atoms) == 0:
            atoms = u.select_atoms(f"protein and segid {chain}")
        residues = atoms.residues
        if len(residues) == 0:
            continue
        first = residues[0]
        last = residues[-1]
        summaries[chain] = {
            "first_resname": first.resname,
            "first_resid": int(first.resid),
            "last_resname": last.resname,
            "last_resid": int(last.resid),
            "n_residues": len(residues),
        }
    return summaries

def select_chains_with_ranges(self, input_path: str, selected_chains: List[str],
                               chain_ranges: Dict[str, List[int]], output_dir: str) -> str:
    """Keep only some chains, each optionally cut to a residue range.

    Args:
        input_path: The structure.
        selected_chains: The chains to keep.
        chain_ranges: `{chain: [first residue, last residue]}`; a chain without a range
            is kept whole.
        output_dir: Where to save the result.

    Returns:
        The new structure.

    Raises:
        ValueError: Nothing matched the selection.
    """
    u = mda.Universe(input_path)
    parts = []
    # Determine whether to use chainID or segid
    use_segid = False
    test_query = " or ".join([f"chainID {c}" for c in selected_chains])
    if len(u.select_atoms(test_query)) == 0:
        use_segid = True
    id_keyword = "segid" if use_segid else "chainID"

    for chain in selected_chains:
        rng = chain_ranges.get(chain, [])
        if rng and len(rng) == 2 and rng[0] is not None and rng[1] is not None:
            q = f"({id_keyword} {chain}) and (resid {rng[0]}:{rng[1]})"
        else:
            q = f"{id_keyword} {chain}"
        parts.append(q)

    full_query = " or ".join([f"({p})" for p in parts])
    atoms = u.select_atoms(full_query)
    if len(atoms) == 0:
        raise ValueError(f"No atoms found for selection: {full_query}")
    output_path = os.path.join(output_dir, "protein_selected_chains.pdb")
    atoms.write(output_path)
    return output_path

    def mutate_with_pymol(self, input_path: str, chain_id: str, residue_number: int, target_residue: str, output_dir: str) -> str:
        """Replace one amino acid with PyMOL's mutagenesis tool.

        PyMOL must be installed and available as the `pymol` command.

        Args:
            input_path: The structure.
            chain_id: Chain of the residue.
            residue_number: Residue number.
            target_residue: New amino acid, three-letter code (e.g. `ALA`).
            output_dir: Where to save the mutated structure.

        Returns:
            The mutated structure.

        Raises:
            RuntimeError: PyMOL failed or wrote no structure.
        """
        input_path = os.path.abspath(input_path)
        output_dir = os.path.abspath(output_dir)
        output_path = os.path.join(output_dir, "protein_mutated.pdb")
        script_path = os.path.join(output_dir, "mutation.pml")

        with open(script_path, "w") as f:
            f.write(f"""
load {input_path}, protein
wizard mutagenesis
refresh_wizard
select mut_target, chain {chain_id} and resi {residue_number}
cmd.get_wizard().do_select("mut_target")
cmd.get_wizard().set_mode("{target_residue}")
cmd.get_wizard().apply()
save {output_path}, protein
quit
""")

        # Execute pymol command line
        result = subprocess.run(
            ["pymol", "-cq", script_path],
            capture_output=True,
            text=True
        )
        if result.returncode != 0:
            raise RuntimeError(f"PyMOL mutagenesis failed: {result.stderr or result.stdout}")

        if not os.path.exists(output_path) or os.path.getsize(output_path) == 0:
            raise RuntimeError("PyMOL did not generate the mutated structure file.")

        return output_path

def get_secondary_structure_mdtraj(self, input_path: str) -> str:
    """The secondary structure of a protein, calculated with DSSP (MDTraj).

    One letter per residue: H (helix), E (strand), C (coil). When DSSP fails, every
    residue is taken as coil.

    Args:
        input_path: The structure.

    Returns:
        The secondary-structure text.
    """
    try:
        traj = md.load(input_path)
        ss = md.compute_dssp(traj, simplified=True)[0]
        ss_string = "".join(ss)
        return ss_string
    except Exception as e:
        # Fallback to all coil sequence matching the length of the protein residues
        u = mda.Universe(input_path)
        n_res = len(u.select_atoms("protein").residues)
        return "C" * n_res

def validate_cg_files(self, pdb_path: str, itp_path: str) -> Tuple[bool, str]:
    """Basic check of uploaded coarse-grained files.

    Both files must exist and not be empty, and the `.itp` must contain a
    `[ moleculetype ]` section.

    Args:
        pdb_path: The coarse-grained structure.
        itp_path: The coarse-grained topology.

    Returns:
        `(ok, message)`.
    """
    if not pdb_path or not os.path.exists(pdb_path):
        return False, "Coarse-grained structure file does not exist."
    if not itp_path or not os.path.exists(itp_path):
        return False, "Coarse-grained topology (.itp) file does not exist."

    if os.path.getsize(pdb_path) == 0:
        return False, "Coarse-grained structure file is empty."
    if os.path.getsize(itp_path) == 0:
        return False, "Coarse-grained topology file is empty."

    # Check if ITP file has [ moleculetype ] directive
    has_moleculetype = False
    with open(itp_path, "r", errors="ignore") as f:
        for line in f:
            if "[moleculetype]" in line.replace(" ", "").lower():
                has_moleculetype = True
                break
    if not has_moleculetype:
        return False, "ITP file does not appear to contain a '[ moleculetype ]' header."

    return True, "Validation successful."

def run_martinize(self, pconfig: ProteinConfig, input_path: str, protein_index: int, output_dir: str) -> Tuple[str, str, str, str, str]:
    """Coarse-grain an atomistic structure with martinize2.

    Args:
        pconfig: The protein's settings (force field, secondary structure, elastic
            network, restraints, disulfide bridges, extra options).
        input_path: The prepared atomistic structure.
        protein_index: Position of the protein (part of the file names).
        output_dir: The protein's work folder.

    Returns:
        `(cg structure, top file, itp file, command, martinize2 output)`.

    Raises:
        RuntimeError: martinize2 failed or wrote no structure.
    """
    input_path = os.path.abspath(input_path)
    output_dir = os.path.abspath(output_dir)
    output_cg = os.path.join(output_dir, f"protein_cg_p{protein_index}.pdb")
    output_top = os.path.join(output_dir, f"protein_p{protein_index}.top")
    output_itp = os.path.join(output_dir, f"molecule_p{protein_index}_0.itp")

    cmd = [
        "martinize2",
        "-f", input_path,
        "-x", output_cg,
        "-o", output_top,
        "-ff", pconfig.forcefield,
        "-name", f"molecule_p{protein_index}"
    ]

    if pconfig.secondary_structure_mode == "MDTraj DSSP":
        ss = self.get_secondary_structure_mdtraj(input_path)
        cmd.extend(["-ss", ss])
    elif pconfig.secondary_structure_mode == "All coil":
        cmd.extend(["-ss", "C"])
    elif pconfig.secondary_structure_mode == "Custom/Precalculated":
        if pconfig.custom_ss_string:
            cmd.extend(["-ss", pconfig.custom_ss_string.strip()])

    if pconfig.use_elastic_network:
        cmd.extend([
            "-elastic",
            "-el", str(pconfig.elastic_lower),
            "-eu", str(pconfig.elastic_upper),
            "-ef", str(pconfig.elastic_force),
        ])

    if pconfig.position_restraints != "none":
        cmd.extend(["-p", pconfig.position_restraints])

    if pconfig.cysteine_bridges:
        cmd.extend(["-cys", pconfig.cysteine_bridges])

    if pconfig.extra_flags:
        cmd.extend(pconfig.extra_flags.split())

    result = subprocess.run(
        cmd,
        cwd=output_dir,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True
    )

    cmd_str = " ".join(cmd)
    if result.returncode != 0:
        raise RuntimeError(f"martinize2 failed with error code {result.returncode}.\nCommand: {cmd_str}\nError output:\n{result.stderr or result.stdout}")

    if not os.path.exists(output_cg) or os.path.getsize(output_cg) == 0:
        raise RuntimeError("martinize2 did not output the coarse-grained structure file.")

    return output_cg, output_top, output_itp, cmd_str, result.stdout

def collect_output_files(self, output_dir: str) -> List[str]:
    """All structure, topology, script, settings and log files in a folder.

    Args:
        output_dir: The folder to search (including sub-folders).

    Returns:
        The file paths.
    """
    files = []
    extensions = [".pdb", ".gro", ".top", ".itp", ".pml", ".json", ".log"]
    for root, _, filenames in os.walk(output_dir):
        for filename in filenames:
            if any(filename.endswith(ext) for ext in extensions):
                files.append(os.path.join(root, filename))
    return files

def create_output_zip(self, config: Config, pconfig: ProteinConfig) -> str:
    # Write config JSON
    """Save the settings and zip the work folder of one protein.

    Args:
        config: The settings of all proteins (written as `martinize_config.json`).
        pconfig: The protein whose work folder is zipped.

    Returns:
        The zip file (`martinize_results.zip` in the work folder).
    """
    output_dir = pconfig.base_folder
    config_path = os.path.join(output_dir, "martinize_config.json")
    with open(config_path, "w") as f:
        json.dump(config.to_dict(), f, indent=4)

    zip_path = os.path.join(output_dir, "martinize_results.zip")
    files = self.collect_output_files(output_dir)

    with zipfile.ZipFile(zip_path, "w", zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as zipf:
        for file_path in files:
            if os.path.exists(file_path) and file_path != zip_path:
                arcname = os.path.relpath(file_path, output_dir)
                zipf.write(file_path, arcname)
    return zip_path

def _named_copies(self, pconfig: ProteinConfig, pdb_path: str, itp_path: str, output_dir: str) -> Tuple[str, str]:
    """Copy the finished files to `cg/<name>.pdb` (or `.gro`) and `cg/<name>.itp`.

    A separate folder is used, so a name that equals an intermediate file (for example a
    downloaded `<PDBID>.pdb`) can never overwrite it.

    Args:
        pconfig: The protein's settings (its `name`).
        pdb_path: The coarse-grained structure.
        itp_path: The coarse-grained topology.
        output_dir: The protein's work folder.

    Returns:
        `(structure, topology)` paths of the copies.
    """
    name = pconfig.name or os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(pdb_path))[0]
    dest_dir = os.path.join(output_dir, "cg")
    os.makedirs(dest_dir, exist_ok=True)
    ext = os.path.splitext(pdb_path)[1] or ".pdb"
    pdb_dest = os.path.join(dest_dir, f"{name}{ext}")
    itp_dest = os.path.join(dest_dir, f"{name}.itp")
    shutil.copy2(pdb_path, pdb_dest)
    shutil.copy2(itp_path, itp_dest)
    return pdb_dest, itp_dest
